cases.why: a game with no score yet is graded anyway, so a partial week records results for games that have not been played
an exactly-50% forecast stops counting as the home pick, so the grade no longer matches the side the card showed
the drift check flags a model for doing significantly BETTER than the backtest, so a good week opens 'Model drift detected'
a z exactly on the threshold stops counting as significant; the rule today is 'at or below -1.96', and this quietly moves the boundary

the standard error is taken from the observed rate instead of the expected one, which is no longer the one-sample test under the null the docstring names, and moves z whenever the two rates are not mirror images
graded backtest seasons are read as live results, so the check compares the backtest with itself and cannot see real drift
the minimum sample is ignored, so two bad games in week 1 can raise a drift issue
a tie goes back to being graded as an away win, so every home pick on a game nobody won scores wrong and every away pick right
the baseline is a typed-in copy again, the old literal's values, so the drift report quotes numbers printed nowhere else and nothing ties them to the backtest: the defect the third audit found.

cases.why: main() compares with a fixed number instead of the file's accuracy, so regenerating the backtest would never move the drift check.
